- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for stabilization.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong downward momentum, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative mid-period; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; apply smoothing (e.g., 5-day EWMA) to reduce noise and avoid overreaction to short-term sentiment swings.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to err on the high side; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7-day mean to anchor forecast.
